title: From Argmax to Strict Unimodality
content:
The parent entry proves that n=5 maximizes the unit n-ball volume ω_n = π^(n/2)/Γ(n/2+1): ω_n ≤ ω_5 for all n. That is a statement about the LOCATION of the maximum only — it is silent on whether the sequence climbs monotonically to that peak or wanders. This file closes that gap by proving STRICT UNIMODALITY: the sequence strictly increases ω_0 < ω_1 < ω_2 < ω_3 < ω_4 < ω_5, and lies strictly below ω_5 for every n ≠ 5. The shape is therefore a single strict hump with no plateaus.

The file imports the parent and reuses its explicit values ω_0=1, ω_1=2, ω_2=π, ω_3=4π/3, ω_4=π²/2, ω_5=8π²/15, its two-step strict-decrease lemma, and its parity-subsequence bounds.
mathContext: Argmax: ∀ n, ω_n ≤ ω_5. Strict unimodality strengthens this to (∀ m<n≤5, ω_m<ω_n) ∧ (∀ n≠5, ω_n<ω_5).
significance: Distinguishes 'where is the max' from 'what is the full monotonicity profile' — the latter is what justifies informal claims like 'ω_4 < ω_5 strictly, with no tie'.

title: The Five Elementary Ascent Steps
content:
Each one-step increase ω_k < ω_(k+1) for k ∈ {0,1,2,3,4} reduces, via the parent's closed forms, to an elementary inequality:
  • ω_0=1 < 2=ω_1 — pure arithmetic (norm_num).
  • ω_1=2 < π=ω_2 — from π > 3 (Real.pi_gt_three).
  • ω_2=π < 4π/3=ω_3 — the gap is π/3 > 0 (only π > 0 needed).
  • ω_3=4π/3 < π²/2=ω_4 — equivalent to 8π < 3π², i.e. 8 < 3π, which holds since π > 3 gives 3π > 9 (nlinarith).
  • ω_4=π²/2 < 8π²/15=ω_5 — equivalent to 15 < 16; NO bound on π is needed (linarith with π² > 0).
The crude π > 3 suffices throughout — the same bound the parent uses for its base cases.
mathContext: Sharpest step ω_4 < ω_5 ⇔ π²/2 < 8π²/15 ⇔ 1/2 < 8/15 ⇔ 15 < 16, independent of π.
significance: Shows the ascent is genuinely cheap: no fine π estimate, no Gamma analysis — just the explicit values and π > 3.

title: Transitivity via Finite Case Split
content: omega_strict_ascent bundles the five concrete steps into the uniform statement: m < n ≤ 5 ⇒ ω_m < ω_n. After introducing the five step inequalities as hypotheses h01,…,h45, the proof does `interval_cases n <;> interval_cases m <;> linarith`. Since n ≤ 5 and m < n, both range over a finite set; each leaf goal ω_a < ω_b (with a < b ≤ 5) is a linear consequence of the chained steps (e.g. ω_0 < ω_3 follows from h01, h12, h23), which `linarith` discharges automatically. This is the cleanest way to turn a chain of adjacent strict inequalities into an order relation over an interval.
mathContext: For a<b≤5, ω_a<ω_b = sum of adjacent gaps (ω_{a+1}-ω_a)+…+(ω_b-ω_{b-1}), each > 0.
significance: Avoids a hand-written induction; the finite range makes case explosion harmless and linarith handles the transitivity bookkeeping.
relatedConcepts: strict monotonicity on a finite set

title: Strict Global Maximum: Two-Sided Closure
content:
omega_five_strict_max proves ω_n < ω_5 for EVERY n ≠ 5, the strict sharpening of the parent's ω_n ≤ ω_5. The case split is on n ≠ 5:
  • n < 5: directly the strict ascent.
  • n > 5: reuse the parent's descent. Split n by parity. Even n = m+m (≥ 6 ⇒ m ≥ 3) is rewritten as 6 + 2(m-3) and bounded by omega_even_le_six then omega_six_lt_five. Odd n = 2m+1 (≥ 7 ⇒ m ≥ 3) is rewritten as 7 + 2(m-3) and bounded by omega_odd_le_seven then omega_seven_lt_five. The `omega` tactic discharges the arithmetic index rewrites.
mathContext: n>5 even: ω_n ≤ ω_6 < ω_5. n>5 odd: ω_n ≤ ω_7 < ω_5. Both subsequences inherit the parent's two-step strict decrease.
significance: Combines the new ascent (n<5) with inherited descent (n>5) into the clean two-sided statement: 5 is the unique strict maximizer.

title: Main Theorem: Strict Unimodality
content: omega_strictly_unimodal packages the two halves into the full monotonicity profile: (∀ m n, m<n→5≥n ⇒ ω_m<ω_n) ∧ (∀ n, n≠5 ⇒ ω_n<ω_5). Read together with the parent's two-step strict decrease (ω_(n+2) < ω_n for n≥5) and the sibling thin-shell limit (ω_n → 0), this completely settles the qualitative shape of the unit-ball-volume sequence: it rises strictly to a unique peak at the 5-ball and then declines strictly within each parity class toward 0. No plateaus, no second hump, a single strict maximizer.
mathContext: ω: ℕ → ℝ is strictly unimodal with mode 5. Verified with 0 sorries, 0 axioms (only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound).
significance: The headline structural result: upgrades 'n=5 is the argmax' to 'the sequence is strictly unimodal', the strongest elementary statement about its shape obtainable without the half-integer Gamma ratio.
